lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Estimate, then count
lessons.intention: We are learning to estimate how many, then count to check.
criteria: I can say how many are in a small group without counting.
I can estimate how many, then count to check.
I can use the words more than, less than and the same.

steps.start: Flash a dice pattern or a few counters for two seconds. How many? How did you know without counting?
steps.teach: Put up to 20 objects in a clear tub. Ask for an estimate, then count together, touching and moving each one. Compare: was it more than, less than or the same as the guess?
steps.practise: Play the firefly game: say how many lit up without counting.
steps.check: Scatter 4 or 5 counters, cover after two seconds: how many? Then estimate a bigger group and check by counting.

lessons.home: Guess how many grapes, pegs or spoons, then count to check.
lessons.vocab: estimate, guess, count, more than, less than, the same
lessons.understand: Why is it fine if your guess wasn't exactly right?
lessons.lookFor: Knows a guess is a sensible estimate, then counting checks it; can say if the count was more or less than the guess.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Counting to 20 and beyond
lessons.intention: We are learning to count objects and say the number sequence forwards and backwards.
criteria: I can count forwards to 30 from any number.
I can count backwards from 20.
I can touch and count objects to 20, and the last number tells me how many.
I know zero means none.

steps.start: Count forwards together from 0 to 30, then start from a different number (7, 12, 18).
steps.teach: Count a set of up to 20 objects, touching and moving each one. Ask: how many altogether? Show that counting in a different order gives the same total. Count back from 20 to 0, and talk about 0 meaning none.
steps.practise: Build the bridge in the Counting Canopy, counting each piece.
steps.check: Give a pile of 14 objects: count them. Then count back from 15.

lessons.home: Count stairs, steps or socks together, forwards and backwards.
lessons.vocab: count, how many, altogether, zero, none, forwards, backwards
lessons.understand: If I count these again starting from a different one, will I get the same number? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Knows the total doesn't change with the order, and that the last number counted tells how many.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Before, after and in between
lessons.intention: We are learning to read, order and find numbers to 20.
criteria: I can recognise numbers from 0 to 20.
I can say the number before, after and in between.
I can put numbers to 20 in order and find missing numbers.
I can use first, second and third.

steps.start: Hold up number cards 0–20 in a muddle. Which do you know?
steps.teach: Peg numbers on a line to 20. Hide one: which is missing? Ask: what comes after 9? before 14? between 11 and 13? Line toys up and use first, second, third.
steps.practise: Bigger or smaller: compare two numbers.
steps.check: Give five number cards to put in order, then ask for the number before and after one of them.

lessons.home: Find house or bus numbers: what comes before and after?
lessons.vocab: before, after, between, first, second, third, order
lessons.understand: How do you know 14 comes after 13 and not before?
lessons.lookFor: Uses the counting order or a number line: after means one more.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Adding and taking away within 10
lessons.intention: We are learning to add and take away by counting on and back.
criteria: I can count on to add and count back to take away.
I can use the signs +, − and =.
I can add and take away in my head to 10.
I can solve a simple missing number problem.

steps.start: Five frame flash: show 3, add 2 more. How many now?
steps.teach: Use counters and a ten frame. Model 4 + 3 by counting on from 4. Model 7 − 2 by counting back. Write each as a number sentence with + − =. Try 5 + ? = 8 with counters hidden under a cup.
steps.practise: Adding within 10, then Taking away within 10.
steps.check: Ask 6 + 3, 9 − 4 and 2 + ? = 7, with counters if needed.

lessons.home: Make up number stories with toys: 3 cars park, 2 more arrive.
lessons.vocab: add, plus, take away, minus, equals, makes, how many left
lessons.understand: Here is 6 + 2. Can you tell me a story that matches it?
lessons.lookFor: Makes up a sensible story: something is added to a group, and the total is bigger.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Doubles and splitting numbers to 10
lessons.intention: We are learning that numbers can be split into parts, and to double.
criteria: I can split 10 into two parts in different ways.
I can double numbers to make up to 10.
I know the total stays the same when I move the parts.

steps.start: Show 5 fingers on one hand and 2 on the other: how many? Do it with different numbers.
steps.teach: Take 10 counters and split them into two groups in every way you can (7 and 3, 6 and 4…). Record them. Then use a mirror or both hands to double 1 to 5.
steps.practise: Hidden fireflies: work out how many are hiding.
steps.check: Ask: 10 is 6 and how many? What is double 4?

lessons.home: Share 10 pasta pieces between two plates in different ways.
lessons.understand: Can 7 be split another way? How many ways can you find?
lessons.lookFor: Finds more than one split (5 and 2, 4 and 3) and sees both parts together make 7.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Sharing equally and halves
lessons.intention: We are learning to share equally and find half.
criteria: I can share a group of things out equally.
I can split a whole into parts and know equal parts are the same size.
I can find half of a shape or a group.

steps.start: Two teddies want to share 6 sweets. Is it fair if one gets 4?
steps.teach: Share objects one at a time onto two plates. Fold a paper shape in half and check the parts match. Show a sandwich cut fairly and unfairly: which is halves?
steps.practise: Share sets of 4, 6, 8 and 10 between two, then between three or four.
steps.check: Show a shape cut into two unequal pieces: is it halves? Why not?

lessons.home: Cut toast or fruit in half at snack time: are the halves the same size?
lessons.vocab: share, equal, fair, half, halves, whole
lessons.understand: Is this half? How do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Checks both parts are the same size or the same number, not just that there are two parts.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Coins and paying up to 10p
lessons.intention: We are learning to know our coins and pay for things up to 10p.
criteria: I can name all the coins to £2.
I can pay the exact amount up to 10p using 1p, 2p, 5p and 10p coins.
I can say if I have given too much, not enough or the right amount.

steps.start: Tip out real or toy coins. Sort them. Which do you know?
steps.teach: Name each coin up to £2. Set up a shop with prices up to 10p. Show paying 7p as 5p and 2p, or seven 1p coins. Talk about giving too much and getting change.
steps.practise: Counting money: add up the coins.
steps.check: Price a toy at 8p: pay for it two different ways.

lessons.home: Let your child pay for something small and talk about the coins.
lessons.vocab: coin, pence, pound, pay, price, change, enough
lessons.understand: Which is worth more, one 5p coin or three 1p coins? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Knows a coin's value isn't how many coins there are: 5p is worth more than 3p.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Days, routines and o'clock
lessons.intention: We are learning about the order of our day, the days of the week and o'clock.
criteria: I can put the events of my day in order.
I can say the days of the week in order and know the months and seasons.
I can read o'clock times on a clock and a digital display.
I know the hour hand and the minute hand.

steps.start: What did you do first today? What happens next? What happens at night?
steps.teach: Order picture cards of a day (wake up, breakfast, school, tea, bed). Say the days of the week and talk about the seasons. On a clock, show the minute hand pointing to 12 for o'clock and move the hour hand.
steps.practise: Telling the time: the o'clock questions.
steps.check: Set 3 o'clock on a clock: what time is it? What day comes after Tuesday?

lessons.home: Point out o'clock times at home and talk about tomorrow's day.
lessons.vocab: o'clock, hour hand, minute hand, morning, afternoon, night, days, months, seasons
lessons.understand: The long hand is on 12 and the short hand is on 3. Is it o'clock? What might you be doing at 3 o'clock in the afternoon?
lessons.lookFor: Explains that the long hand on 12 means o'clock and the short hand shows the hour, and links the time to a real part of their own day.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Longer, heavier and holds more
lessons.intention: We are learning to compare sizes and measure with everyday things.
criteria: I can compare length, height, weight and how much things hold.
I can use longer, shorter, taller, heavier, lighter, more and less.
I can estimate and then measure with things like cubes or hand spans.

steps.start: Which is taller, you or the door? Which is heavier, a book or a feather?
steps.teach: Compare two pencils (longer/shorter), two bags (heavier/lighter using hands as a balance), and two cups of water (holds more/less). Estimate how many cubes long a book is, then measure.
steps.practise: Measure three objects in cubes or hand spans and put them in order.
steps.check: Give two objects: which is longer? How many cubes long is it?

lessons.home: Baking: talk about full, empty, more and less when measuring.
lessons.vocab: long, short, tall, heavy, light, full, empty, more, less, measure
lessons.understand: How could we check which is longer fairly?
lessons.lookFor: Lines the ends up together, or uses the same thing to measure both.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Copying and continuing patterns
lessons.intention: We are learning to copy, continue and make patterns.
criteria: I can copy and continue a pattern with objects, shapes or numbers.
I can make my own pattern.
I can find missing numbers on a number line to 20.

steps.teach: Make a red–blue–red–blue bead pattern. Continue it, then make AAB patterns. Count in ones along a number line and find gaps.
steps.practise: Number patterns: find the next number.
steps.check: Show a pattern with a gap: what is missing?

lessons.home: Spot patterns on clothes, tiles and fences.
lessons.understand: What comes next? How do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Names the part that repeats and uses it to say what comes next.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Sorting 2D shapes and 3D objects
lessons.intention: We are learning to name, describe and sort shapes.
criteria: I can name common 2D shapes and 3D objects.
I can describe them as straight, round, flat or curved.
I can sort shapes in different ways.

steps.start: Feely bag: describe a shape you can feel without looking.
steps.teach: Name circle, square, triangle, rectangle; cube, sphere, cone, cylinder. Sort them: flat or not, rolls or not, straight or curved sides.
steps.practise: 2D shapes: name the shape and count the sides.
steps.check: Give three shapes to name and say one thing about each.

lessons.home: Go on a shape hunt in the kitchen or on a walk.
lessons.vocab: circle, square, triangle, rectangle, cube, sphere, cone, cylinder, flat, curved
lessons.understand: Is this still a triangle if I turn it round? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Knows turning a shape doesn't change it: it still has 3 sides and 3 corners.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Position, direction and symmetry
lessons.intention: We are learning words for position and direction, and to make symmetrical pictures.
criteria: I can use in front, behind, above, below, left, right, forwards and backwards.
I can follow and give simple directions.
I can make a picture with one line of symmetry.

steps.start: Simon says: put your hand above your head, behind your back.
steps.teach: Hide a toy and give directions to find it. Fold paper, paint on one side and press to make a symmetrical butterfly.
steps.practise: Give the pupil directions to move a toy on a grid, then swap roles.
steps.check: Where is the cup? (in front of / behind the book). Is this picture the same on both sides?

lessons.home: Play a hide-and-seek game giving directions.
lessons.vocab: in front, behind, above, below, left, right, forwards, backwards, symmetry
lessons.understand: Hide a toy and give me clues with words like behind, under and next to. Which clue helped me most? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Chooses position words to suit a new hiding place, and can say which clue helped and why.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Sorting and simple charts
lessons.intention: We are learning to sort things and show what we found.
criteria: I can sort objects by colour, shape or size.
I can ask a question and collect answers.
I can make a picture chart where one picture is one thing.
I can answer questions about a simple chart.

steps.start: Sort a pile of buttons or toys: how did you sort them?
steps.teach: Ask family members their favourite fruit. Show each answer with one picture. Which has most? Least? Count tally marks in fives.
steps.practise: Tally marks: count them in fives.
steps.check: Look at a picture chart: which has the most? How many like apples?

lessons.home: Sort the washing or toys and count each group.
lessons.vocab: sort, group, most, least, chart, tally
lessons.understand: What does our chart tell us? Which has the most?
lessons.lookFor: Reads the chart to answer a question, not just describing the pictures.
